Design and develop products that change the world with a master's or Ph.D. in mechanical engineering
Mechanical engineers drive the design and development of cutting-edge technology, affecting the livelihood of others. From wave energy to devices that assist agricultural needs, Oregon State offers endless possibilities. Our faculty are excellent instructors and leaders in their fields, tackling real-world issues.
Students in mechanical engineering can focus on advanced manufacturing, design, renewable energy, and more. Graduate tracks include Master of Engineering, Master of Science, and PhD in mechanical engineering. While obtaining a degree, graduates attend conferences, work with industry, and connect with other students, leading to fulfilling careers.

Admissions Process
Admissions Process
The School of Mechanical, Industrial, and Manufacturing Engineering brings together great students and inspiring faculty on a campus equipped to promote innovation and excellence in its research endeavors. MIME has a strong commitment to recruit engineers who believe firmly in engineering for good.
Fully funded graduate research assistantships for highly qualified candidates are available across a number of projects.
If Oregon State is your preferred choice for graduate study, and you believe that you have superior qualifications, then we encourage you to apply. Admission is very competitive. The most successful applicants over the years:
had GPAs above 3.50 on a 4.00 scale
submitted a Statement of Purpose demonstrating alignment of their and their intended supervisor’s research
had published as an author or co-author on academic publication(s)
Highly qualified applicants may be offered a graduate research assistantship or graduate teaching assistantship.
Read More Info
Application Deadlines
M.S. / Ph.D. Priority Application Deadline: December 15
M.S. / Ph.D. Final Application Deadline: January 31
MEng Final Application Deadline: January 31
If you wish to be included in the consideration pool for a graduate assistantship, you must complete and submit your application by the priority deadline. Applications submitted after this deadline will be considered after the priority application pool review ends; they will not receive priority review.
Graduate Assistantships
Graduate Assistantships
Each year, faculty win externally competitive research grants. These grants support graduate research assistant positions. When faculty are actively recruiting M.S. and/or Ph.D. students to work on projects funded by these grants, a brief synopsis of the research project will be listed on the webpage linked below.
Please note that not all faculty who are hiring have projects listed below. If you are considering graduate school, we encourage you to apply. Faculty who are hiring will reach out to you individually if your application is of interest to them.

Master of Science Requirements
Master of Science Requirements
Master of Science Mechanical Engineering student at Oregon State pursue one of the following degree paths:
Thesis
Students whose M.S. degree includes a thesis are involved in original mechanical engineering research or the novel application of existing mechanical engineering knowledge to a practical problem. A student’s research topic must be approved and supervised by their major professor and their work will be evaluated by their graduate committee. After successfully defending their thesis at a final oral examination, students will be required to register their research title with the Office of Graduate Education and upload to ScholarsArchive their thesis for approval and archiving.
Non-thesis
Students whose M.S. degree includes work not leading to a thesis, will fulfill the Graduate School’s research-in-lieu-of-thesis requirement by completing a project applying mechanical engineering knowledge and methods to a practical problem. A student’s project topic must be approved and supervised by their major professor and their work will be evaluated by their graduate committee. A project report will be presented at a final oral exam, but project reports are not reviewed or approved by the Office of Graduate Education.
View Requirements
Master of Engineering Requirements
Master of Engineering Requirements
Strengthen your technical credentials with a Master of Engineering
The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professional, coursework-only degree designed for individuals seeking practical skills and leadership roles in industry. The program does not require a thesis or research project, allowing students to focus on advanced coursework aligned with their professional goals and job-related skill development.
MEng vs. M.S. Degrees
The Master of Science (M.S.) degree is research-oriented and suited for students interested in advanced technical research or pursuing a Ph.D., typically requiring a thesis or research project. In contrast, the MEng is a course-based degree intended for students who want to apply advanced engineering knowledge in industry without completing a thesis. Read more about the difference between an MEng and an MS degree.
Learn about MEng vs M.S.
MEng Degree Requirements
Oregon State’s MEng program requires 45 credits of advanced coursework, which may include core engineering courses, ethics, technical writing, and elective courses relevant to professional interests. Students typically develop a Program of Study with an advisor during their first term and complete a final portfolio in place of a final oral exam.
View detailed MEng requirements
Paying for your MEng
MEng students are generally self-funded. While all students may apply for graduate research or teaching assistantships, these opportunities are highly competitive and more commonly awarded to Ph.D. and M.S. students. Additional funding options include scholarships, grants, fellowships, loans, and employer tuition reimbursement programs. Learn more about paying for your MEng degree.
Explore MEng payment options
How to Apply
Apply to a Master of Engineering program online through the Office of Graduate Education. MEng degree admission requirements basically align with the minimum academic requirements for admission into all Oregon State graduate programs. This typically looks like having a four-year baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university with a cumulative B average. The GRE is not required for admission to an MEng degree.
Deadlines
The mechanical engineering MEng program admits students for a fall term start date.
Application deadline: January 31

Ph.D. Degree Requirements
Ph.D. Degree Requirements
Doctoral students in mechanical engineering generate new knowledge through original research. Dissemination of the new knowledge happens in the form of a doctoral thesis (dissertation). A student’s research topic must be approved and supervised by their major professor and their work will be evaluated by their graduate committee.
After successfully defending their dissertation at a final oral examination, students will be required to register their research title with the Graduate School and upload their thesis to ScholarsArchive for approval and archiving.
View Requirements
Graduate Minor Requirements
Graduate Minor Requirements
To be eligible to earn a minor in Mechanical Engineering students must have previously taken at least one course in each of the following preparatory areas: linear algebra, calculus-based statistics, engineering economy and computer programming. Courses for the minor in may be taken on 100 percent on campus or a combination of on campus and online.
